Forgiveness means…

Forgiveness means trusting God to provide justice and relinquishing the desire for personal retribution and vindication. Forgiveness is a choice which may or may not be supported by emotions.

God is big enough to handle our situations and circumstances.

God tells us : Dear friends, never take revenge. Leave that to the righteous anger of God. For the Scriptures say, “I will take revenge;     I will pay them back,”     says the Lord. Instead, “If your enemies are hungry, feed them.     If they are thirsty, give them something to drink. In doing this, you will heap     burning coals of shame on their heads.” Don’t let evil conquer you, but conquer evil by doing good.

One obstacle to forgiveness is the issue of seeking justice. Maintaining an attitude of forgiveness while seeking justice may be difficult. Determining when and how to seek justice can be determined by the “peace” principle. “And let the peace that comes from Christ rule in your hearts.” If one can seek justice while maintaining an attitude of forgiveness and peace, then it may be appropriate to seek intervention from a higher authority.

Forgiveness is an action that both bears and requires repetition. When one finds that resentment and bitterness is being harbored, one must forgive again.

Sometimes it is helpful to understand one’s own thought process. In the case of something being stolen, often all that is wanted is the return of what has been taken, not retribution or vindication for the act of stealing. Forgiveness doesn’t mean that justice cannot be sought. Forgiveness means that ultimate justice comes from God.

One prime example of forgiveness is Jesus’ example on the cross: “Father, forgive them for they know not what they do.”

When is forgiveness appropriate? 1. violation of moral absolutes. 2. wrongful deprivation of resources. 3. wrongful causation of suffering.

To clarify, delayed gratification is appropriate in many situations. Delayed gratification may cause short term deprivation of resources or short term “suffering.” To illustrate, saving of resources may feel like deprivation but the long term outlook is an increase in resources. Discipline may feel like suffering but the long term outlook is improved performance and less suffering.

When the individual releases feelings of hatred, disappointment, bitterness, and resentment to God, the stress of judicial responsibility is released. God is placed in His rightful place as judge. By forgiving, stress is minimized, one’s attitude is more positive and the opportunity for personal growth is maximized. As Lewis B. Smedes wrote, “When you release the wrongdoer from the wrong, you cut a malignant tumor out of your inner life. You set a prisoner free, but you discover that the real prisoner was yourself."

Another step that can be helpful is to maintain an attitude of gratefulness. By choosing to be grateful, one can focus on the positive rather than the negative.

Maintaining an attitude of forgiveness and gratitude leads to a more fulfilling life. “Don’t let evil conquer you, but conquer evil by doing good.”
